evidence.title: Replit: The Project Editor
evidence.finding: The hosted Project Editor provides Agent chat, project tools, live preview and a task board in the browser.

evidence.title: Replit: Mobile features; Navigate your project
evidence.finding: Native iOS and Android clients support Agent, Tools and Tasks panes, project continuation and completion or help notifications.

evidence.title: Replit: Agent modes
evidence.finding: Replit Agent has Free, Power and Max modes; Auto routes paid work to models. Model routing does not establish support for a third-party coding harness.

evidence.title: Replit: Agent billing
evidence.finding: Replit plan credits pay for Agent and other cloud services; paid actions use effort-based pricing after confirmation.

evidence.title: Replit: Getting started; Import code and design
evidence.locator: Getting started; Import code and design
evidence.finding: Start a project by describing an idea in plain language, or bring it in from GitHub, Figma or uploaded files, in the cloud Project Editor. The page names no templates and does not itself state that no local environment is needed.

evidence.title: Replit: How background tasks work
evidence.finding: A main-thread prompt can create titled tasks with descriptions and plans, or users can start a planning thread.

evidence.title: Replit: Plan your tasks; Review and accept
evidence.locator: Plan your tasks; Review and accept
evidence.finding: Agent proposes detailed plans and definitions of done; users inspect View plan, accept tasks or request a revised plan before execution.

evidence.title: Replit: Create and approve remaining tasks; Let Agent schedule the work
evidence.locator: Create and approve remaining tasks; Let Agent schedule the work
evidence.finding: Agent identifies prerequisite tasks and queues dependent work until the prerequisite is applied. The board shows the blocker.

evidence.title: Replit: Your app is safe while tasks run
evidence.locator: Your app is safe while tasks run
evidence.finding: Each background task inherits the project context and receives its own Agent and project copy.

evidence.title: Replit: Import code and design
evidence.finding: Projects can begin from GitHub, Figma or uploaded files; this establishes input channels, not verified architecture comprehension.

evidence.title: Replit: What is the task system; Frequently asked questions
evidence.locator: What is the task system; Frequently asked questions
evidence.finding: Native tasks have Drafts, Active, Ready and Done states, a board, separate threads and explicit acceptance. Draft planning sessions can be archived and restored; cancelling building work discards it.

evidence.title: Replit: What is the task system
evidence.finding: Agent can split a request into tasks and put them on the human-visible task board.

evidence.title: Replit: Tasks start running; Availability
evidence.finding: Core supports one active background task, Pro up to ten and Enterprise up to sixty-four. Additional tasks queue.

evidence.title: Replit: Let Agent schedule the work
evidence.finding: Agent schedules independent tasks when capacity exists and holds dependent tasks until prerequisites are applied.

evidence.title: Replit: What is the task system; Review and apply
evidence.locator: What is the task system; Review and apply
evidence.finding: Replit Agent decomposes a request into background Agent tasks with separate threads and returns work logs, tests and previews to the main-version review flow.

evidence.title: Replit: How Routines run; Availability and limits
evidence.locator: How Routines run; Availability and limits
evidence.finding: Paid-plan chat Routines repeat hourly, daily or weekly without a new request. They run in Power or Max, queue behind other chat work and do not schedule publishing.

evidence.title: Replit: Frequently asked questions
evidence.finding: Cancel stops building and discards its work. The main thread and each task thread permit follow-up direction.

evidence.title: Replit: Board view
evidence.finding: A project board displays Drafts, Active, Ready and Done tasks alongside task conversations. Fleet-scale navigation has not been tested.

evidence.title: Replit: Plan mode; What you can build
evidence.locator: Plan mode; What you can build
evidence.finding: Users start with ordinary chat, refine plans and let Agent create task lists before approving work.

evidence.title: Replit: Frequently asked questions
evidence.finding: The cloud Project Editor saves files, history and the running app when the browser closes. This documents cloud persistence, not an unlimited Agent process lifetime.

evidence.title: Replit: Tasks start running
evidence.finding: Background tasks run in isolated project copies and do not change the main version until applied. The docs do not name these copies as containers, VMs or worktrees.

evidence.title: Replit: What happens when I close my browser?
evidence.locator: What happens when I close my browser?
evidence.finding: Files, history and running app are preserved in the cloud for a later visit. No worker-crash recovery test was performed.

evidence.title: Replit: What is Replit Agent?
evidence.finding: Agent sets up the project and infrastructure. Specific dependency-cache, port-collision and clean-remote-host behavior remains untested.

evidence.title: Replit: Control spending
evidence.finding: Core and Pro Routines have per-run budgets checked after each step; an in-progress step can complete beyond the budget. Enterprise lacks the per-run budget.

evidence.title: Replit: Review and apply
evidence.finding: Finished tasks expose a work log, test results and preview; active threads and board cards show task status.

evidence.title: Replit: Viewing Agent usage
evidence.finding: Agent billing is effort-based and uses plan credits shared with cloud services. A controlled reconciliation against provider billing was not performed.

evidence.title: Replit: Tasks start running
evidence.finding: Plan-based task limits cause additional background tasks to queue until slots are available. This is not evidence of per-host CPU or RAM scheduling.

evidence.title: Replit: Personal vs. team workspaces
evidence.finding: Team workspaces share projects with members; Core includes five collaboration seats and Pro fifteen. Simultaneous co-prompt ordering is not established by this source.

evidence.title: Replit: Personal vs. team workspaces; Managing members
evidence.locator: Personal vs. team workspaces; Managing members
evidence.finding: Personal workspaces have an admin and project guests; team workspaces add members with access to all workspace projects. Admins can invite and remove members.

evidence.title: Replit: Configure single sign-on
evidence.finding: SAML SSO requires Enterprise and organization/identity-provider admin access. SSO does not automatically invite users; invitations or SCIM manage membership.

evidence.title: Replit: Review and accept; Review and apply
evidence.locator: Review and accept; Review and apply
evidence.finding: Humans approve plans before background execution and apply or dismiss finished changes before they affect the main version.

evidence.title: Replit: Review and apply
evidence.finding: Ready tasks expose a work log, test results and live preview with Apply or Dismiss decisions. Review effort and missed evidence were not measured.

evidence.title: Replit: Review and apply
evidence.finding: Task review retains a work log, test results and a live preview in the task flow. A cross-task artifact gallery was not established.

evidence.title: Replit: App Testing
evidence.finding: With App Testing enabled, Agent periodically tests apps it builds in an actual browser and fixes issues it finds; it is available for Full Stack JavaScript and Streamlit Python web apps. Documentation is not proof of mandatory independent review or an enforced passing test gate.

evidence.title: Replit: Apply changes safely
evidence.finding: Applying tasks invokes AI-assisted conflict resolution. The source does not establish a GitHub PR workflow.

evidence.title: Replit: How do I publish my app?
evidence.locator: How do I publish my app?
evidence.finding: Users publish to a live URL from the Project Editor. Production authorization and revision binding were not tested.

evidence.title: Replit: What happens if Agent makes a mistake?

evidence.finding: Agent creates checkpoints that users can roll back to when a change is wrong.

evidence.title: Replit: Import code and design

evidence.title: Replit: Model improvement

evidence.title: Replit: What you get; Limitations

evidence.title: Replit: Starter Plan

evidence.title: Replit: What is the Replit Desktop App; install and sync
evidence.locator: What is the Replit Desktop App; install and sync
evidence.finding: The current first-party desktop guide explicitly offers a native app for Windows, Mac and Debian-based Linux, including Agent, Project Editor and publishing. This establishes desktop clients rather than inferring them from a companion CLI.

evidence.title: Replit: From your browser or mobile phone
evidence.locator: From your browser or mobile phone
evidence.finding: The first-party AI code editor page explicitly offers the full cloud development workspace from a browser on desktop or mobile devices, alongside the native mobile apps.

evidence.title: Replit: Build locally; Isolate builds in local sandboxes
evidence.locator: Build locally; Isolate builds in local sandboxes
evidence.finding: The current desktop product page explicitly says Agent can build and run apps using the local environment and selected local folders. On supported Windows and macOS devices it names Microsoft Execution Containers for code/build-tool isolation. This does not establish a Linux local-execution sandbox.

evidence.title: Replit: Compare deployment options; Full BYOC warning and availability
evidence.locator: Compare deployment options; Full BYOC warning and availability
evidence.finding: Full BYOC includes Agent/development execution in a customer tenant but is explicitly private preview, with eligibility/configurations confirmed through Enterprise onboarding. Published-app BYOC and Image Exports are early access and do not move the development/Agent control plane. Even Full BYOC leaves the control plane external and explicitly is not an entirely self-hosted or air-gapped Replit installation.

evidence.title: Replit: Sandbox architecture; draft PR and review workflow
evidence.locator: Sandbox architecture; draft PR and review workflow
evidence.finding: The current repository-contribution guide explicitly says the development sandbox runs in a microVM. Replit owns the contribution workflow: it creates a branch, commits/pushes changes, opens a GitHub draft PR or GitLab MR, and updates the request after review.

evidence.title: Replit: Changes and pull requests
evidence.finding: The product Changes pane switches between local changes and linked pull requests, shows branch/description details and renders the proposed code diff with added/removed lines. Linked requests also appear in Details and review feedback can be addressed through Agent.

evidence.title: Replit: Can I use my own API keys with Agent?
evidence.locator: Can I use my own API keys with Agent?
evidence.finding: The first-party FAQ separates app API credentials from the Agent itself: user provider keys in Secrets power calls made by the built app, while the Agent experience uses Replit-managed model infrastructure rather than the user-key route. Curated in-product model selection is separate from replacing that infrastructure with an independently keyed endpoint. Replit AI billing charges its own plan credits. This is not evidence of a third-party coding harness or a native subscription-login path.

evidence.title: Replit: Replit Ownership; limited access rights
evidence.finding: The current service terms reserve all rights in the Replit Service and related software to Replit and give users only the expressly granted limited access rights. This classifies the main Agent/platform as proprietary, separately from user-created code and any separately licensed public client/SDK components.

evidence.title: Replit: Build with teammates; independent threads and shared board
evidence.locator: Build with teammates; independent threads and shared board
evidence.finding: Distinct invited teammates can start their own Agent threads and tasks in the same project, share the board, view history and review/apply ready work. The guide emphasizes separate threads; it does not establish multiple humans sending instructions into the same active Agent conversation/work item.

evidence.title: Replit: Tiered monthly credits; up to 15 builders; no per-user fees
evidence.locator: Tiered monthly credits; up to 15 builders; no per-user fees
evidence.finding: The current Pro documentation explicitly supplies a flat recurring team plan with tiered monthly credits and up to 15 builders, with no per-user fees. Core/Pro subscriptions and usage credits are documented; one-off credit-pack top-ups are prepaid consumption rather than a one-time software license.

evidence.title: Replit: Monthly/Yearly Core, Pro and Enterprise plan offering
evidence.locator: Monthly/Yearly Core, Pro and Enterprise plan offering
evidence.finding: The current public plan offering lists recurring Core and Pro subscriptions and an Enterprise sales plan. It does not offer the whole ADE free without a paid tier or a one-time software license. The page defaults to annual-billing display; this pass does not convert annual prices or infer a USD monthly price from a dollar sign.

evidence.title: Replit: Pricing catalog module 596139; Core default monthly Stripe price and USD allocation
evidence.locator: Pricing catalog module 596139; Core default monthly Stripe price and USD allocation
evidence.finding: The immutable first-party script loaded by the public pricing page defines the non-legacy default Core monthly price as 2000 cents with a 20-USD monthly allocation. The old 2500-cent option is explicitly legacy-only. Annual pricing and restricted regional Core offers are separate entries. This establishes the default public Core plan at USD 20 per month without converting an annual rate.
